requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware, software frameworks, target models, and datasets required to reproduce EAGLE-3 are available and correctly configured.
Core deep learning and inference framework dependencies (PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers, SGLang, vLLM) are installed at versions compatible with the EAGLE-3 evaluation pipeline.
Code has been implemented that installs PyTorch and HuggingFace Transformers with pre-allocated KV cache support, forming the baseline vanilla autoregressive decoding environment used by all methods.

verification.spec: Run `python -c 'import torch, transformers; print(torch.__version__, transformers.__version__)'` and verify both import successfully. Additionally, verify that a baseline vanilla autoregressive decoding script exists that loads a HuggingFace causal LM with pre-allocated KV cache (e.g., use_cache=True, past_key_values pre-allocated as tensors) and can generate tokens from a prompt.

verification.spec: Run `python -c 'import sglang; print(sglang.__version__)'` and verify the version string equals '0.4.4' (or that the installed sglang package version matches v0.4.4).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that installs vLLM as the production-grade serving framework for throughput evaluation on A100/RTX3090 (Table 5).

verification.spec: Run `python -c 'import vllm; print(vllm.__version__)'` and verify it imports without error and reports a valid version string.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vanilla autoregressive baseline implementation is verified to use HuggingFace Transformers models with the PyTorch backend and pre-allocated KV cache, producing a 1.00x speedup reference point.

verification.spec: Import the vanilla decoding baseline module. Instantiate a target model via HuggingFace transformers (AutoModelForCausalLM), confirm PyTorch backend (isinstance of torch.nn.Module), and confirm KV cache is pre-allocated (inspect model.generate config or custom cache tensor shapes prior to first token). Run one short generation and confirm output tokens/sec is recorded and used as the 1.00x reference baseline.

verification.spec: Inspect the training loop and verify torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ (or an equivalent gradient-clipping call) is invoked with max_norm=0.5 before the optimizer step.

verification.spec: Inspect the training config/script and verify the AdamW optimizer is constructed with lr=5e-5 (i.e., 0.00005).

Assert config.hidden_size equals 5120 for Vicuna-13B, 4096 for LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, 8192 for LLaMA-3.3-70B-Instruct, and 4096 for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B. sub_tasks.requirements: The extraction and fusion of low, middle, and high-level features from the target model into vector g via concatenation and an FC layer is correctly implemented, following Section 3.1 and Figure 5.
Multi-layer feature extraction from the target model correctly identifies and hooks into the low, middle, and high-level decoder layers to produce feature sequences l, m, and h.
Code has been implemented to register forward hooks (or otherwise capture activations) on three specific decoder layers of the target model, corresponding to low, middle, and high-level features.

verification.spec: Load the target model, register the feature-extraction mechanism used by EAGLE-3, and verify that exactly three activation sites (low, middle, high) are hooked/read from the target model's decoder layers. Assert that running a single forward pass yields three distinct captured tensors (l, m, h).

sub_tasks.requirements: The indices of the low, middle, and high layers are chosen to reflect low-level (near-input), middle (roughly mid-depth), and high-level (near-output) representations of the target model rather than three arbitrary or identical layers.

verification.spec: Inspect the layer indices chosen for l, m, h in the config/code. Assert that (i) the three indices are distinct, (ii) the low index is in the first third of the target model's decoder depth, the middle index near the mid-depth, and the high index in the last third, matching the paper's description of low/middle/high-level features.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each extracted feature tensor l, m, h has shape [batch, seq_len, hidden_size] matching the target model's hidden dimension k, verified for a sample forward pass.

verification.spec: Run a forward pass on the target model with a small batch (e.g., batch=2, seq_len=8) and assert that each captured tensor l, m, h has shape [2, 8, hidden_size] where hidden_size equals the target model's config.hidden_size (k).

sub_tasks.requirements: Feature extraction is compatible with the prefill phase and with the verification stage's forward pass so that l, m, h from generated tokens are available to the draft model in subsequent drafting steps.

verification.spec: Simulate the full inference loop: (1) run prefill on the target model and confirm l,m,h are captured for prefix tokens; (2) run one verification-stage forward pass with new tokens and confirm l,m,h for those new positions are appended and accessible to the draft model in the next drafting step.

sub_tasks.requirements: The concatenation and FC fusion module correctly combines l, m, h into the fused feature g of dimension k.
Code has been implemented that concatenates l, m, and h along the feature dimension to produce a 3k-dimensional tensor per token position.

verification.spec: Create synthetic l, m, h tensors of shape [B, T, k] with distinct known values, run the fusion concat function, and assert the output has shape [B, T, 3k] with the correct sub-slices matching l, m, h respectively along the last dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: A dedicated fully connected (FC) layer with input dimension 3k and output dimension k is defined as part of the draft model and applied to the concatenated (l, m, h) vector to produce g.

verification.spec: Instantiate the EAGLE-3 draft model class and access the fusion FC layer (e.g., model.fc or model.feature_fc). Assert it is an instance of torch.nn.Linear with in_features == 3*k and out_features == k where k equals the target model's hidden_size. Verify by running the layer on a dummy tensor of shape [1, 4, 3k] and checking output shape is [1, 4, k].

sub_tasks.requirements: The fusion FC layer's weights are trainable parameters registered in the draft model's parameter list so they are updated during draft-model training.

verification.spec: Instantiate the draft model and locate the fusion FC layer (3k->k). Assert that its weight parameters appear in draft_model.parameters(), have requires_grad=True, and are included in the optimizer parameter group used by the training script.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a synthetic input where l, m, h are known tensors, running the fusion module produces an output g with shape [batch, seq_len, k] equal to FC(concat(l, m, h)), verified by a unit-style check.

verification.spec: Create synthetic tensors l, m, h each of shape [2, 5, k] with fixed random seed. Pass them through the fusion module (concat then FC). Independently compute expected = fc_layer(torch.cat([l,m,h], dim=-1)). Assert torch.allclose(fusion_module(l,m,h), expected) and that the output shape equals [2, 5, k].

sub_tasks.requirements: The fused feature g is integrated into the draft model's Step-1 input pipeline together with the token embedding e as described in Figure 5.

In Step 1 of drafting, the draft model input is formed by concatenating g (from the target model) with the embedding e of the sampled token along the feature dimension, producing a 2k-dimensional vector per position.

verification.spec: Instrument the draft model's Step 1 forward path to capture the tensor fed into the input-projection FC. For a batch with known g (shape [B, T, k]) and known token-embedding e (shape [B, T, k]), verify the captured tensor equals torch.cat([g, e], dim=-1) with shape [B, T, 2k]. Assert exact equality (torch.equal).

sub_tasks.requirements: A second FC layer (input dim 2k, output dim k) inside the draft model reduces the concatenated (g, e) input back to k dimensions before feeding it into the single Transformer decoder layer.

verification.spec: Instantiate the draft model and locate the input-projection FC layer that consumes concat(g, e). Assert weight shape is [k, 2k] (or equivalent nn.Linear(2k, k)). Feed a synthetic tensor of shape [B, T, 2k] and confirm the output has shape [B, T, k] and is passed as input to the single decoder layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: The embedding e used in the draft-model input is obtained from the target model's token embedding table (shared or copied), not from a separately initialized embedding.

verification.spec: Compare the draft model's token embedding weight tensor byte-for-byte against target_model.get_input_embeddings().weight. Assert they are either the same object (shared) or numerically identical (copied), not randomly initialized.

sub_tasks.requirements: For draft steps beyond Step 1, the pipeline correctly substitutes the draft model's own output a for the unavailable g of unverified positions.

In Step 2 and later, positions whose tokens have not yet been verified by the target model use the previous-step draft output a in place of g, while already-verified positions continue to use the fused g from the target model.

verification.spec: Simulate a two-step draft with a prefix of 2 verified tokens. Instrument the draft-model forward to log the source (g vs a) at each position. Assert positions 0..1 use g (from target), and the third position (unverified) uses a from Step 1's output. Repeat with a longer prefix to confirm the pattern.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vector a produced by the draft-model decoder layer has the same dimensionality k as g so it is a drop-in replacement in the concat-with-embedding input pipeline.

verification.spec: Run one draft-model forward pass on a synthetic input of shape [B, T, k]. Assert the decoder-layer output tensor 'a' has shape [B, T, k] matching the target model's hidden size, so it can be substituted for g in the next step's concat-with-embedding input.

sub_tasks.requirements: The EAGLE-3 draft model (single Transformer decoder layer with FC input projection and LM head) and its multi-step drafting pipeline replacing g with self-produced a in later steps is correctly implemented.
The draft model architecture (single Transformer decoder layer preceded by an FC input projection and followed by the target model's LM head) is implemented.
Code has been implemented for a draft model class whose core module is exactly one Transformer decoder layer (self-attention + FFN) matching the hidden size k of the target model.

verification.spec: Introspect the EAGLE-3 draft model class. Enumerate its submodules and confirm exactly one Transformer decoder layer instance (e.g., a LlamaDecoderLayer or equivalent containing self-attention + FFN). Assert its hidden_size attribute equals the target model's hidden_size k. Confirm there is no stack of multiple decoder layers (count == 1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an FC input projection layer that maps a 2k-dimensional concatenation of a k-dimensional feature (g or a) and a k-dimensional token embedding down to k dimensions before the decoder layer.

verification.spec: Locate the FC input projection layer in the draft-model code and assert it is nn.Linear(2*k, k) (or equivalent). Confirm it is invoked on concat([g_or_a, e], dim=-1) inside the draft model forward, before the decoder layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: The draft model uses the target model's LM head (shared/frozen weights) to convert its decoder output a into a token distribution rather than a separately learned head.

verification.spec: Locate the LM head used by the draft model to project 'a' to token logits. Assert its weight tensor is the same object (or numerically identical) as target_model.lm_head.weight. Also verify requires_grad is False (frozen) during draft-model training.

sub_tasks.requirements: The draft model's decoder layer output a has dimension k (target hidden size) so that it can substitute for g in subsequent drafting steps.

verification.spec: Run the draft model's decoder layer on a synthetic input [B, T, k] and assert its output tensor has last-dim = target_model.config.hidden_size (k). Then feed that output back as 'a' into a second draft step's concat-with-embedding path and confirm shapes match without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unlike EAGLE, the EAGLE-3 draft model does NOT include a feature-prediction output head or feature-regression loss branch; the only training signal used at inference-facing outputs is token prediction via the LM head.

verification.spec: Inspect the training loss function used for EAGLE-3 (grep/read the training script). Verify it contains only a token-level cross-entropy loss (l_token) computed via the target model's LM head applied to the draft outputs, and that no l_fea / feature-regression / smooth-L1-on-features term is added. Also inspect the draft model definition and confirm there is no separate 'feature head' output projection distinct from the shared LM head.

sub_tasks.requirements: The FC layer that reduces the concatenated (l, m, h) 3k-dimensional per-position vector to a k-dimensional fused feature g is wired as input to the draft model pipeline.

verification.spec: Given synthetic l, m, h tensors of shape [B, T, k] populated with distinct sentinel values, invoke the fusion concat routine and assert output shape is [B, T, 3k] with each k-sized slice equal to l, m, h respectively along the last dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a linear (FC) layer projecting the 3k-dimensional concatenated vector down to the k-dimensional fused feature g used as draft-model input at Step 1.

verification.spec: Locate the fusion FC (3k->k) layer in the draft-model code. Assert it is an nn.Linear whose in_features == 3*k and out_features == k, and that it is invoked on the 3k-dimensional concat(l,m,h) tensor to produce g used at Step 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The multi-step drafting pipeline correctly uses g at Step 1 and the draft model's own output a in place of g for all subsequent steps, concatenated with the sampled token's embedding.

verification.spec: Simulate Step 1 drafting: for a prefix of length T, provide fused features g of shape [1, T, k] and embeddings e of shape [1, T, k]. Run the draft model and assert (i) inputs are concatenated to [1, T, 2k], (ii) passed through the input FC to [1, T, k], (iii) through the decoder layer producing a of shape [1, T, k], (iv) LM head applied yields a next-token distribution.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that at Step 2 the draft model input at the newest position is the concatenation of a_{t+1} (from Step 1's draft-model output) and the embedding e of the token sampled at Step 1, rather than any g from the target model.

verification.spec: Run drafting Step 1 to obtain a_{t+1} and a sampled token 'x'. Then in Step 2, instrument the draft-model input construction for the newest position and assert its input equals concat(a_{t+1}, embed(x)), NOT concat(g_x, embed(x)). Confirm no target-model fused feature is queried for token x.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that at Step 3 and any later drafting step, the newest-position input concatenates the previous step's a with the embedding e of the token sampled at that previous step, and no g is ever looked up for un-verified tokens.

verification.spec: Extend the simulated draft loop to Step 3 and Step 4. At each step, assert the newest-position input is concat(a_prev, embed(token_prev)) where a_prev is the draft output from the immediately preceding step and token_prev was sampled from the LM head at that step. Assert no g_target lookup occurs for unverified positions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The draft model samples the next token from the LM head applied to a at each step and feeds that token's embedding back into the next step's input, matching the pipeline in Figure 5.

verification.spec: Run a multi-step chain draft. At each step, verify the code path: (i) compute a via draft decoder, (ii) logits = target_lm_head(a), (iii) sample token from logits, (iv) look up its embedding, (v) feed embed + a into the next step's input. Assert this pipeline matches Figure 5's flow.

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV cache of the draft model's decoder layer is maintained across drafting steps so that previously computed prefix positions (using g) are reused when new positions (using a) are appended.

verification.spec: Run a two-step draft with KV-cache enabled in the draft-model decoder layer. Record the K/V tensors after Step 1. In Step 2, verify that (a) the cached K/V from prefix positions (computed with g) are reused without recomputation, and (b) only the new position's K/V (computed from a) is appended. Assert cache length grows by exactly 1 per step.

sub_tasks.requirements: The drafting-stage control logic (draft depth, chain-vs-tree drafting for measurement modes) is implemented consistent with the paper's settings.

verification.spec: Inspect EAGLE-3 drafting configuration and assert max draft tree depth == 8. For 7B/8B, 13B, 70B classes, assert total draft-token budgets match EAGLE-2's per-class values (60, 50, 48 respectively) and expansion selects 10 nodes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a chain-drafting mode (no tree branching) used when measuring n-alpha acceptance rates, in which each step produces a single token fed forward as the next input.

verification.spec: Invoke the drafting routine with a 'chain' mode flag (used for n-alpha acceptance rate measurement). Assert that at each step exactly one token is generated (top-1 or sampled) and fed as the sole input to the next step, with no tree branching or multiple candidate children created.

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral checks confirming that the drafting pipeline produces consistent shapes, uses a not g for un-verified positions, and matches expected token generation on a controlled input.

On a fixed prefix (e.g., 'How can'), a single-step drafting pass produces exactly one candidate next-token distribution per prefix position with output tensors of shape (prefix_len, vocab_size) from the LM head applied to a.

verification.spec: Instantiate the EAGLE-3 draft model, run a single Step-1 forward pass on a short prefix (e.g., 'How can') with the fused features g and token embeddings e as input, and assert the resulting logits tensor after the LM head has shape (prefix_len, vocab_size) and that exactly one distribution is produced per prefix position (no extra tokens, no batch collapse).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that at drafting Step k>=2 the input tensor to the input FC contains the previously produced a (not any fused g) at the newest position, checked by tensor identity/equality against the Step 1 output cached in memory.

verification.spec: Run drafting for at least 2 steps. Cache the Step 1 output tensor a1. Instrument Step 2 to capture the raw input to the input-projection FC. Slice off the newest-position feature half (first k dims of the 2k concat) and assert torch.equal(newest_feature, a1_at_newest_position). Also assert this feature is NOT equal to any g computed by the target model on the drafted token (which should not have been called).

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test confirms that if the draft model's Step 1 output a is manually replaced with the true target-model g for that token, the Step 2 draft-token distribution changes, demonstrating the pipeline actually uses a as the substitute for g.

verification.spec: Run drafting Step 1 to obtain a and the resulting Step 2 draft-token logits L_a. Then force-run the pipeline again but manually overwrite the newest-position feature entering Step 2 with the target-model-computed g for that token; capture the new Step 2 draft-token logits L_g. Assert L_a != L_g (i.e., torch.allclose returns False under a reasonable tolerance like atol=1e-4), demonstrating the draft pipeline actually consumes a as the substitute.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured behavior of the draft-model pipeline: acceptance-rate stability across drafting steps consistent with Figure 7.

With LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B as target on MT-bench in chain-drafting mode, EAGLE-3's acceptance rate n-alpha remains approximately flat from n=0 through n=7 (in contrast to EAGLE's decline), consistent with Figure 7.

verification.spec: Run EAGLE-3 with LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B target on MT-bench in chain-drafting mode (no tree), measure n-alpha for n=0..7 as defined in Section 4, and check that max(n-alpha) - min(n-alpha) over n in [0,7] is small (approximately flat) matching Figure 7 (approximately 0.75-0.80 across n).

sub_tasks.paper_unit: max-min gap in acceptance rate over n=0..7

sub_tasks.requirements: The training-time test procedure (simulated multi-step draft rollouts with modified attention mask, direct token prediction loss only, no feature prediction loss) is correctly implemented with the specified optimizer, learning rate, gradient clipping, and target-model-generated responses.
The training loop simulates multi-step draft generation by feeding the draft model's own outputs back as inputs across additional training steps (training-time test).

Code has been implemented to perform an initial (Step 1) forward pass through the draft model using target-model features g concatenated with token embeddings e as input, producing draft output vectors a.

verification.spec: Inspect the draft model source and confirm the Step-1 forward pass concatenates target-model fused features g with token embeddings e, passes through an FC reducer to hidden size k, and feeds through a decoder layer to produce output vector a. Execute a unit test that constructs synthetic g and e tensors and verifies non-None output vector a with shape (seq_len, k).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to perform simulated Step 2 and Step 3 rollouts during training that replace the target-model feature at draft positions with the draft model's own previous output a, concatenated with the corresponding embedding of the sampled token.

verification.spec: Trigger the training-step forward for two simulated steps and inspect that Step-2 input at draft positions is (a_prev, e_sampled_token) rather than (g, e), and Step-3 input is (a_from_step2, e_sampled). Assert via monkey-patched hooks that g is not used at simulated positions in steps 2 and 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: The training procedure supports at least two simulated test steps (rollout depth) as depicted in Figure 6, with the outputs of each step fed back as inputs to the next step.

verification.spec: Configure the training loop with rollout depth >= 2 and confirm that during a single training iteration the draft model is invoked at least 3 times (native + 2 simulated) with outputs of each step feeding the next. Use a counter/hook to record invocation count and input provenance.

sub_tasks.requirements: During simulated rollout steps, the draft-model outputs a are detached-or-processed such that gradients propagate through each test step consistently with the training-time test formulation (no unintended stop-gradient breaking the multi-step objective).

verification.spec: Run one training forward+backward on a small batch and assert that gradients flow into the draft model parameters through outputs produced in each simulated test step (i.e., grads become non-zero after backprop from step-2 and step-3 losses in isolation via masking). No unintended .detach() should cut the multi-step objective.

sub_tasks.requirements: The self-attention mask used during training-time test is modified to reflect the tree-like contextual relationship between original training tokens and the simulated draft-step tokens (Figure 6).
For the native (first) training step the attention mask is a standard lower-triangular causal mask over the original training sequence.

verification.spec: Extract the attention mask used for the native (first) training step and assert it is a standard lower-triangular boolean/additive causal mask over the original sequence length (e.g., torch.tril of ones).

sub_tasks.requirements: For simulated Step 2 / Step 3 inputs (draft-generated tokens), queries only attend to (i) their corresponding-position original training-data keys (lower-triangularly) and (ii) diagonally to their own predicted-token keys, matching the mask pattern shown in Figure 6.

verification.spec: Construct the training-time-test attention mask for a length-3 original sequence with 2 simulated draft steps (total 9 query positions: 3 original + 3 step2 + 3 step3). Assert that (a) the 3x3 block over original queries and original keys is a standard lower-triangular mask (allowed), (b) each simulated-step query attends to original-training keys in a lower-triangular pattern up to its corresponding position, and (c) attention among simulated-step keys is strictly diagonal (a step-2 query only attends to its own step-2 key at the same position, not to other step-2 keys). Compare the built mask elementwise against a hand-coded ground-truth matrix from Figure 6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that attention between simulated-step queries and other simulated-step keys is restricted to the diagonal (a token attends to itself in that step but not to other same-step siblings), avoiding cross-contamination between parallel branches.

verification.spec: Extract the attention mask used between simulated-step queries and simulated-step keys and assert that the sub-block corresponding to same-step siblings is diagonal (only self-attention on the diagonal, off-diagonal entries masked out), matching the pattern in Figure 6.

sub_tasks.requirements: The attention computation for the diagonal-only interactions between simulated-step queries and simulated-step keys is implemented via vector dot-products (or an equivalent sparse form) rather than a full dense matmul, to avoid the computational waste noted in Section 3.2.

verification.spec: Inspect the attention implementation for the training-time-test path; confirm that same-step query-key interactions are computed via elementwise multiplication + sum along the head dim (vector dot products) or a sparse/gather form, rather than a full dense (Q @ K^T) followed by masking. A behavioral check compares wall-clock or FLOPs against a naive dense variant on a small input.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test / behavioral check verifies that the constructed training-time-test attention mask matches the expected pattern in Figure 6 for a small toy sequence (e.g., length 3 with 2 simulated steps).

verification.spec: Write a unit test that instantiates the mask-building utility for seq_len=3 and num_simulated_steps=2, and asserts torch.equal(built_mask, expected_mask) where expected_mask is a hard-coded 9x9 boolean tensor derived directly from Figure 6 (original triangular block + per-simulated-step triangular attention to original keys + diagonal attention among each simulated step's own keys).

sub_tasks.requirements: The training loss is direct token-prediction loss only; the EAGLE feature-prediction loss l_fea has been removed.

Code has been implemented so that the training objective computes only a token-level loss l_token (e.g., cross-entropy / KL against the target model's next-token distribution) at each of the training and simulated rollout steps.

verification.spec: Instantiate the EAGLE-3 training loss module and run a forward/backward pass on a small synthetic batch. Assert that the loss returned corresponds to a token-level objective (cross-entropy or KL between draft logits and target next-token distribution) computed at each simulated rollout step. Verify by inspecting the loss computation graph (torch.autograd) that gradients flow only through token-level terms, and that summing the per-step token losses reproduces the total loss within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: No feature-regression term (e.g., MSE / SmoothL1 between draft-model output a and target-model top-layer feature f) is included or back-propagated in the EAGLE-3 training loss.

verification.spec: Statically inspect the EAGLE-3 training loss source code (grep/AST-parse) for any MSE, SmoothL1, or L1/L2 term between draft outputs (a) and target top-layer features (f). Additionally run a training step with a hook that records all tensors contributing to the backward graph, and assert none of them corresponds to a feature-regression term. Test passes iff no such term exists.

sub_tasks.requirements: The token-prediction loss is applied to the outputs of both the native step and every simulated test step (so multi-step draft outputs receive supervision).

verification.spec: Instrument the training loss computation and assert that a non-zero token-prediction loss term is computed for the native step AND each simulated step. Zeroing out the outputs of any single step should reduce the total loss, confirming all steps contribute supervision.

sub_tasks.requirements: The optimizer, learning-rate, and gradient-clipping hyperparameters specified in Section 4 Implementation are correctly configured.
The training code uses the AdamW optimizer.

verification.spec: Inspect the training script and assert that the optimizer instantiated is torch.optim.AdamW (or equivalent).

sub_tasks.requirements: AdamW is configured with betas (beta1, beta2) = (0.9, 0.95).

verification.spec: Assert that the AdamW optimizer is constructed with betas=(0.9, 0.95).

sub_tasks.requirements: The learning rate is set to 5e-5.

verification.spec: Assert that the optimizer learning rate is 5e-5 as configured in the training script/CLI defaults.

sub_tasks.requirements: Gradient clipping is applied with a maximum gradient norm of 0.5.

verification.spec: Inspect the training loop and assert that torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ (or equivalent) is invoked with max_norm=0.5 before optimizer.step().

sub_tasks.requirements: Training data is produced by invoking the target model to generate responses to prompts (rather than using the raw fixed dataset responses).
Code has been implemented that, for each training prompt, runs the target LLM to generate a response which is used as the training target sequence.

verification.spec: Run the data-preparation pipeline on a handful of ShareGPT prompts and confirm that for each prompt the target LLM is invoked (e.g., via .generate) and its produced response is saved as the training target sequence (not the original ShareGPT completion).

sub_tasks.requirements: During generation of training data, the multi-layer features (l, m, h) and top-layer hidden states from the target model are captured and stored/used as supervision signals or as inputs for the draft model.

verification.spec: During target-model generation, verify (via hooks on the target model) that hidden states from designated low, middle, and high layers are captured and either serialized to disk or passed into the draft model input pipeline. Assert tensors of shape (seq_len, hidden_size) for each of l, m, h are produced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The target-model-generated responses (not the original human-written completions) are the sequences over which the draft model's token-prediction loss is computed.

verification.spec: Inspect a training batch and confirm that the token-loss labels correspond to the target-model-generated response tokens, not the original ShareGPT/UltraChat human-written completion. A simple check: hash of label sequences equals hash of the target-generated responses stored during data prep.

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end training pipeline (data loading, forward with masked attention, multi-step rollout, loss, optimizer step) runs correctly and produces a usable draft model.

A training entry-point script exists that ties together the target-model data generation, the training-time-test forward pass, the token loss, the AdamW optimizer with the specified hyperparameters, and gradient clipping, and can be launched to train an EAGLE-3 draft model.

verification.spec: Execute the top-level training entrypoint (e.g., `python train_eagle3.py --config ...`) end-to-end for a few steps and confirm it wires together: (a) target-model data generation or preloaded features, (b) training-time-test forward with rollout>=2, (c) token loss, (d) AdamW(lr=5e-5, betas=(0.9,0.95)), (e) grad clip 0.5. The run must exit cleanly with a saved checkpoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: A short (smoke) training run completes without error and the token-prediction loss decreases over iterations, confirming that gradients flow through both the native step and the simulated test steps.

verification.spec: Launch a short smoke training run (e.g., 200 iterations on a small subset) and verify the run finishes without error and that the mean token-prediction loss over the last 20 iterations is lower than the mean over the first 20 iterations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Training logs record per-step token loss (and optionally per-simulated-step loss) so that the effect of training-time test on multi-step acceptance can be diagnosed.

verification.spec: Inspect the training logs directory (or stdout capture) after a short training run and assert that per-step token loss values are recorded (e.g., in a jsonl/tensorboard/log file), with distinguishable entries per training iteration.

sub_tasks.requirements: The behavioral outcome of the training-time-test procedure (as claimed in Figure 4 / Figure 7) is realized: adding the training-time test keeps the multi-step (n>=1) acceptance rate n-alpha nearly flat rather than dropping sharply as in EAGLE.

After training with the full training-time-test procedure, the resulting draft model's 1-alpha acceptance rate on MT-bench with LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B is substantially higher than an ablation trained without the training-time test (i.e., 'EAGLE without fea pred' variant in Figure 4), matching the qualitative gap shown in Figure 4.

verification.spec: Train two EAGLE-3 draft models for LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B: (A) full training-time test and (B) 'EAGLE without fea pred' (no simulated steps). Evaluate 1-alpha acceptance rate on MT-bench in chain-drafting mode. Assert acceptance_rate_1_alpha(A) - acceptance_rate_1_alpha(B) >= 0.1 (per Figure 4 qualitative gap).

sub_tasks.requirements: For the trained EAGLE-3 draft model, the acceptance rate n-alpha on MT-bench (LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B) stays approximately constant across n = 0..7 (per Figure 7), rather than degrading like EAGLE.

verification.spec: Evaluate the trained EAGLE-3 draft model with LLaMA-Instruct 3.1 8B on MT-bench in chain-drafting mode, computing n-alpha for n=0..7. Assert max_n(n-alpha) - min_n(n-alpha) <= 0.08 (approximately flat, per Figure 7).

sub_tasks.requirements: The EAGLE-2-style context-aware dynamic draft tree, tree attention verification, and speculative sampling acceptance criterion (lossless) are correctly integrated into EAGLE-3.
The dynamic draft tree construction (EAGLE-2 style) is implemented for EAGLE-3, including expansion, confidence-based scoring, and pruning.
Code has been implemented that constructs a tree-shaped draft (rather than a chain) where multiple candidate tokens can be produced at each position by the draft model.

verification.spec: Invoke the drafting routine on a single prefix and verify the returned draft data structure represents a tree: multiple candidate tokens at at least one position (branching factor > 1), and the tree has depth > 1. Assert that at least one node has multiple children.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses the draft model's output probabilities (confidence) to approximate acceptance rates and score candidate paths in the draft tree.

verification.spec: During draft-tree construction, inspect that node scores are computed from the draft model's softmax probabilities (confidence) — e.g., as cumulative product of probabilities along the path — and used to rank candidate paths. Hook into the scoring function to confirm it consumes draft logits/probs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs an expansion phase selecting the top-scoring nodes for further expansion (10 nodes per expansion step as specified in Appendix A).

verification.spec: During draft-tree expansion, log the number of nodes selected at each expansion step and assert it equals 10 (as specified in Appendix A for EAGLE-2 setup, inherited by EAGLE-3).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs a final pruning step at the end of the drafting stage, retaining only the highest-scoring paths / nodes for verification.

verification.spec: Inspect the drafting-stage code and confirm a pruning function is invoked at the end of drafting that ranks candidate tree nodes/paths by score (draft-model confidence) and retains only the top-K, discarding the rest before verification. Verify by constructing a synthetic draft tree with known scores and asserting only top-scoring nodes remain.
verification.paper_cite: Section 2.2 (EAGLE-2 dynamic draft tree with pruning)

sub_tasks.requirements: The draft tree depth is configurable and set to 8 for EAGLE-3 (increased from 6 used by EAGLE-2), while the number of retained nodes matches the EAGLE-2 defaults per model size (60 for 7B/8B, 50 for 13B, 48 for 70B).

verification.spec: Load the EAGLE-3 inference config and assert draft_tree_depth == 8; assert total_draft_tokens equals 60 for 7B/8B, 50 for 13B, 48 for 70B target models. Confirm these are exposed as configurable parameters.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dynamic draft tree adapts its shape to context: given different prefixes, the produced tree structures (branching pattern and depth used) differ rather than following a single fixed template.

verification.spec: Run the EAGLE-3 drafting stage on two different prefixes with clearly different token distributions (e.g., structured code vs free-form prose) and record the produced draft-tree adjacency structure. Assert the two tree structures differ in branching pattern or effective depth, confirming context-dependence.

sub_tasks.requirements: Tree attention verification pass is implemented, enabling parallel verification of all draft tree candidates by the target model in a single forward pass.
Code has been implemented that constructs a tree attention mask reflecting the parent-child relationships of nodes in the dynamic draft tree, so each token attends only to its ancestors in the tree.

verification.spec: Construct a small draft tree with a known parent-child structure, call the tree-attention-mask builder, and assert the resulting boolean mask has True at (i,j) iff node j is an ancestor of node i (or i==j), and False otherwise.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that constructs position ids for draft tree tokens consistent with each token's depth in the tree, so rotary/positional encodings behave correctly under tree attention.

verification.spec: Construct a draft tree with nodes at various depths, call the position-id builder, and assert each token's position_id equals (prefix_length + depth_in_tree). Verify that sibling nodes share the same position_id and that a subsequent forward pass with these ids yields consistent rotary embeddings.

sub_tasks.requirements: The target model performs a single forward pass over the entire draft tree with the tree attention mask and returns per-node probabilities used to evaluate all candidates in parallel.

verification.spec: Run the verification stage on a draft tree with N nodes and assert: (a) exactly one target-model forward pass is invoked (e.g., by patching the model call and counting), (b) the returned logits tensor has N positions, one per tree node, (c) the tree attention mask is passed to the forward call.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, after target-model verification, extracts the KV cache entries and hidden features corresponding to the accepted path so the next draft/verify cycle can resume from the correct target-model state.

verification.spec: After a verification cycle that accepts a specific path in the draft tree, assert the target-model KV cache retains entries only for the accepted-path positions (not for rejected sibling nodes) and that the low/mid/high-level fused features for the accepted path are stored for reuse. Confirm subsequent decoding step produces identical logits as if the accepted tokens had been generated sequentially.

sub_tasks.requirements: The lossless speculative sampling acceptance criterion is correctly integrated with the tree draft for EAGLE-3.

Code has been implemented that, for each candidate draft token t_hat along a selected tree branch, computes the acceptance probability min(1, p(t_hat) / p_hat(t_hat)) using the target-model probability p and the draft-model probability p_hat recorded at drafting time.

verification.spec: Feed a fixed draft token with known draft-model probability p_hat and target-model probability p into the acceptance routine; assert the computed acceptance probability equals min(1, p/p_hat) within floating point tolerance across several (p, p_hat) test values.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, on rejection of a draft token, samples a replacement token from the normalized distribution norm(max(0, p - p_hat)) and discards remaining draft tokens along that branch.

verification.spec: Force a rejection (e.g., set p_hat > p for target token) and assert: (a) the replacement token is sampled from a distribution equal (up to float tolerance) to normalize(max(0, p - p_hat)), verified by Monte Carlo over many trials with a fixed seed, and (b) remaining draft tokens along that branch are discarded from further consideration.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under greedy decoding (temperature=0), the acceptance criterion reduces to accepting a draft token iff it matches the target-model argmax at that position, and on mismatch the target-model argmax replaces it.

verification.spec: Set temperature=0 and run the acceptance routine on a mix of matching and non-matching draft tokens; assert that a draft token is accepted iff it equals argmax(target_logits) at that position, and on rejection the accepted replacement equals argmax(target_logits).

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end EAGLE-3 generation with dynamic draft tree + tree attention verification + acceptance criterion is losslessly equivalent in output distribution to vanilla autoregressive decoding of the target model (verified by producing identical greedy outputs at temperature=0 on a small held-out set of prompts).

verification.spec: On a held-out set of ~20 prompts, run vanilla autoregressive greedy decoding and EAGLE-3 greedy decoding (temperature=0) with the same target model and seed; assert output token sequences are byte-identical for every prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: The verification stage integrates cleanly with the drafting loop, yielding correct multi-token generation per cycle and measurable acceptance behavior.

Code has been implemented that alternates drafting (dynamic tree construction by the draft model) and verification (parallel tree-attention forward pass by the target model) in a loop until an end-of-sequence or maximum length is reached.

verification.spec: Invoke the top-level generate() with a prompt and max_new_tokens=64; patch the draft-model and target-model call sites to record call order and assert the sequence alternates draft-then-verify repeatedly, terminating on EOS or max length.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that logs, per verification cycle, the number of tokens accepted from the draft (used to compute the average acceptance length tau).

verification.spec: Run generation on a short prompt and inspect the returned metrics/logs; assert a list or counter of per-cycle accepted-token counts is exposed and that its mean equals the reported tau within numerical precision.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a chain-like (non-tree) draft configuration for computing n-alpha acceptance rates, matching the evaluation setup used to report acceptance rates in Figures 4 and 7.

verification.spec: Confirm a config flag (e.g., use_tree=False or chain_mode=True) exists that switches the drafting stage to produce a single linear chain of draft tokens; run in this mode and assert the draft structure has no branching (each node has at most one child), and that n-alpha acceptance-rate collection is enabled.

sub_tasks.requirements: The speedup ratios and average acceptance lengths reported in Table 1 across all 4 target models, 5 datasets, and both temperatures=0 and =1 are reproduced within tolerance.
Evaluation harness for measuring speedup ratio and average acceptance length is correctly implemented.

Code has been implemented that measures wall-clock speedup ratio as the ratio of tokens-per-second of the accelerated method to tokens-per-second of vanilla autoregressive decoding on the same hardware with pre-allocated KV cache.

verification.spec: Run vanilla autoregressive decoding and the accelerated method on the same prompts/hardware with pre-allocated KV cache; assert the speedup ratio returned by the benchmark utility equals (tokens_accel/time_accel) / (tokens_vanilla/time_vanilla) within float tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes average acceptance length tau as the mean number of tokens generated per draft-verify cycle, counting all accepted draft tokens plus the bonus verified token.
